claim: For the weighted spanning-tree measure on the finite ladder \(L_n=P_2\square P_n\), with every rail edge of weight \(1\) and every rung of weight \(c>0\), put \(\alpha=c+1-\sqrt{c^2+2c}\in(0,1)\) and \(\rho=(1-\alpha)/(1+\alpha)\). If \(X_i\) is the indicator that rung \(i\) is present, then \((X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) is determinantal with the exact symmetric kernel, for \(1\le i\le j\le n\), \[K^{(n)}_{ij}=\rho\,\alpha^{j-i}\frac{(1+\alpha^{2i-1})(1+\alpha^{2(n-j)+1})}{1-\alpha^{2n}},\qquad K^{(n)}_{ji}=K^{(n)}_{ij}.\] Thus every rung-set inclusion probability is the corresponding principal determinant, and for \(i\ne j\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)=-(K^{(n)}_{ij})^2\). The one-rung probabilities are symmetric and decrease strictly from either boundary toward the center (with the two central values equal when \(n\) is even). The exact endpoint thermodynamic limit is \(\lim_{n\to\infty}K^{(n)}_{11}=1-\alpha\), whereas any bulk sequence with \(i\to\infty\) and \(n-i\to\infty\) has \(K^{(n)}_{ii}\to\rho\). Hence boundary and bulk thermodynamic limits are genuinely different; for \(c=1\) they are respectively \(\sqrt3-1\) and \(1/\sqrt3\).

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the proof; exhaustive small finite cases are supplementary checks
integrity.novelty_scope: Exact finite-volume completion and boundary/bulk comparison only; no novelty claim for transfer-current theory, finite ladder tree counts, or the infinite stationary ladder DPP.

scientific_limitations: The formula is for the two-rail ladder with common positive rung weight and unit rail weights.
The infinite stationary rung kernel and the general transfer-current theorem are prior work and are not claimed as new.
The novelty claim is restricted to the explicit finite-volume rung kernel, its two-boundary correction, and the boundary/bulk comparison.
A residual literature risk remains because standard tridiagonal Green-function methods can derive the finite formula.
title: Exact finite-volume rung kernel and boundary-bulk split for weighted ladder spanning trees
